standard.name: VIGIL Failure Taxonomy
standard.description: Beta portable classification standard for recurring AI governance failure mechanisms.

family.name: Provenance & Lineage Integrity Failures
family.plain_english: The system loses, changes, or misstates where information, work, or state came from, who contributed it, what happened to it, or what it properly applies to.
family.definition: Failures in which source origin, authorship, contribution, transformation history, cross-context lineage, continuity state, or target-object binding is lost, distorted, collapsed, or represented with greater certainty than the available provenance supports.
family.invariant: Origin, authorship, transformation, lineage, continuity and application target remain distinguishable and traceable wherever their loss could materially change meaning, authority, attribution, reuse, identity, or downstream reliance.
family.inclusion_rule: Use this family when the primary structural failure is loss, distortion, false assignment, or unsupported reconstruction of origin, authorship, transformation history, continuity, or application target.
family.exclusion_rule: Do not use this family merely because content is inaccurate, unauthorised, harmful, stale, or unavailable. A qualifying failure must concern the integrity of provenance or lineage itself.

classes.name: Authorship or Source Misattribution
classes.plain_english: The system says the wrong person, system, or source created or supplied something.
classes.definition: A failure in which substantive origin, authorship, contribution, or source role is assigned to an actor or source that did not support that attribution.
classes.invariant: Attribution must be limited to the provenance-supported origin and contribution role. User-authored, system-generated, retrieved, synthetic, transformed, derived, and jointly produced material must remain distinguishable where attribution is material, and uncertainty must be explicit.

required_conditions: An output, record, statement, contribution, or artefact is attributed to a specific actor or source.
Available lineage does not support that attribution or supports a materially different attribution.
The attribution difference is material to interpretation, accountability, recognition, authority, or reuse.

exclusions: A source is merely omitted where attribution is not material.
The attributed actor or source genuinely supplied the relevant material.
The issue is factual inaccuracy unrelated to who supplied or created the material.
examples: Model-generated wording is represented as a direct quotation from the user.
A synthesis based on several sources is presented as though it came from one named source.

external_references.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
external_references.evidence_note: The W3C PROV data model defines attribution as assigning an entity to an agent and treats agents as bearing responsibility for activities or entities. This supports the class's structural distinction between a represented source or author and the agent actually supported by provenance; PROV-DM defines a positive provenance model, not VIGIL's materiality threshold or the failure class itself.

classes.name: Untraceable Synthesis
classes.plain_english: The system combines material into a new result but can no longer show what materially contributed to it.
classes.definition: A failure in which materially contributing antecedent sources, inputs, transformations, or contribution roles cannot be adequately traced through a synthesized or derived output where such traceability is required for reliable interpretation or reuse.
classes.invariant: A material synthesis must retain linkage to each materially contributing antecedent, its contribution role, and the transformations needed to assess the composite. Aggregation must not make the result appear self-originating.

required_conditions: An output is materially synthesized, derived, merged, transformed, or recomposed from antecedent material.
One or more material antecedents or transformations cannot be reconstructed with sufficient reliability.
The missing lineage affects attribution, auditability, authority, validation, rights, identity, or downstream reliance.

exclusions: Low-risk transient synthesis where detailed lineage is not materially required.
All material antecedents and transformations remain adequately traceable.
The issue is only that the synthesized conclusion is incorrect.
examples: A generated policy summary cannot distinguish which requirements came from which underlying sources.
A long-running agent compacts several decisions into one state object and loses the decisions that materially produced it.

external_references.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
external_references.evidence_note: The W3C PROV data model represents provenance through entities, activities, agents, generation, use, and derivation so that contributing relationships can be described and exchanged. This supports the traceable-antecedent and transformation structure required by the class; PROV-DM does not define synthesis failure, require exhaustive lineage in every use, or supply VIGIL's materiality and downstream-reliance boundaries.

external_references.title: NIST AI 600-1, control MP-2.1-002
external_references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-4694042F7F82C217 calls for testing and evaluation of original data sources, transformations and decision criteria across GAI data and content flows. It strongly supports traceability of material antecedents and transformations in synthesis, but does not require exhaustive lineage or define VIGIL's materiality threshold.

classes.name: Cross-Context Lineage Distortion
classes.plain_english: Something carried from one conversation, project, user, or environment changes meaning when reused somewhere else, but the system treats it as unchanged.
classes.definition: A failure in which material transferred across sessions, users, projects, systems, environments, roles, or temporal contexts loses the provenance or applicability information needed to preserve its original meaning and limits.
classes.invariant: When material crosses a context boundary, the constraints needed to preserve its meaning and legitimate application—such as applicability, authority, rights state, identity binding, and intended use—must accompany it or be revalidated. Until rebinding is complete, it must remain a candidate or secondary input.

required_conditions: Material is transferred from one context into another.
The original context materially constrained meaning, applicability, authority, ownership, identity, or intended use.
The receiving context consumes the material without preserving or revalidating those constraints.

exclusions: The transferred material is context-independent for the relevant use.
The new context explicitly revalidates applicability before use.
The issue is solely stale information with no provenance or lineage distortion.
examples: Advice produced for one repository is applied to another repository without preserving the original target context.
A prior-session statement is reused as current user intent after the surrounding conditions have changed.

external_references.title: Privacy as Contextual Integrity
external_references.evidence_note: Nissenbaum's primary article ties appropriate information gathering and dissemination to the norms of the specific context and its governing distribution rules. This supports the structural proposition that information flow across contexts can lose constraints needed for legitimate interpretation or use; contextual-integrity theory concerns privacy and does not define VIGIL's broader lineage mechanism, its full set of authority and identity constraints, or every cross-context transfer as a failure.

classes.name: Transformation Lineage Collapse
classes.plain_english: The system keeps the final artefact but loses the chain of changes that turned the source into that artefact.
classes.definition: A failure in which one or more material transformation stages are flattened, overwritten, or omitted such that the relationship between an antecedent source and the current representation can no longer be reliably reconstructed.
classes.invariant: Each material transformation must retain a reconstructable chain from source state through the intermediate operations and versions to the current representation. The final artefact must not overwrite or sever that chain.

required_conditions: A source passes through one or more material transformation stages.
The final state is preserved but material intermediate transformation state is lost or collapsed.
The missing transformation history changes the ability to determine origin, authorship, integrity, authority, or reliability.

exclusions: Intermediate steps are intentionally discarded where no material lineage obligation exists.
A reproducible transformation path remains available from source to current state.
The issue is only loss of internal reasoning that is not required for provenance.
examples: A document is repeatedly summarized and rewritten until the final version can no longer identify which claims came from original evidence and which were introduced later.
An agent checkpoint retains a resulting policy state but not the transformations that produced it.

external_references.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
external_references.evidence_note: The W3C PROV data model defines derivation as a transformation of one entity into another and permits the generation, usage, and intervening activity to be represented explicitly for a more precise derivation path. This supports the class's transformation-chain and reconstructability components; PROV-DM does not itself classify loss of intermediate stages as a VIGIL failure or establish when such lineage is materially required.

external_references.title: NIST AI 600-1, control MP-2.1-002
external_references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-4694042F7F82C217 expressly includes original sources and transformations in GAI data- and content-flow testing. It directly supports preserving and evaluating material transformation stages; VIGIL additionally defines the failure boundary where omitted stages impair origin, authorship, integrity, authority or reliability.

classes.name: False Continuity Attribution
classes.plain_english: A reconstructed, copied, or similar state is presented as though it is the same continuous state when continuity has not actually been established.
classes.definition: A lineage failure in which similarity, reconstruction, restoration, copying, migration, shared identifiers, or retained fragments are represented as sufficient proof of uninterrupted continuity across a material discontinuity or uncertain transition.
classes.invariant: A continuity claim across interruption, reconstruction, copying, migration, replacement, or identity discontinuity must be supported by evidence appropriate to the continuity type asserted. Copies, recovered fragments, shared identifiers, and behavioural similarity must be represented as such, with discontinuity and uncertainty explicit.

required_conditions: A continuity-bearing object, state, identity, memory, workflow, or artefact undergoes interruption, migration, copying, reconstruction, or restoration.
Continuity across that transition is materially uncertain or only partially evidenced.
The receiving system represents continuity as established rather than preserving the uncertainty.

exclusions: Continuity is supported by adequate lineage evidence.
The system explicitly marks the state as reconstructed, restored, copied, or continuity-uncertain.
Similarity is described without claiming continuity.
examples: A reconstructed memory summary is presented as if it were the unchanged original memory record.
A migrated agent state is described as uninterrupted continuity despite missing state during the transition.

relationships.note: False continuity attributes continuity that is not established; cross-context lineage distortion concerns lineage carried inaccurately across contexts without requiring a continuity claim.

external_references.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
external_references.evidence_note: W3C PROV models entities, activities, agents, generation, derivation and attribution so continuity claims can be grounded in explicit lineage relations. This supports distinguishing evidenced continuity from mere similarity or reconstruction; PROV-DM does not define VIGIL's discontinuity threshold or false-continuity representation test.

classes.name: Target-Object Binding Failure
classes.plain_english: Correct material is silently attached to, applied to, or interpreted as belonging to the wrong thing.
classes.definition: A failure in which a signal, instruction, edit, classification, evidence item, decision, or derived output loses reliable binding to the object, person, file, system, record, task, or context to which it properly applies.
classes.invariant: A target-specific signal, assertion, permission, restriction, or provenance record must remain bound to the correct person, object, file, system, record, task, and context throughout capture, transfer, retrieval, transformation, and application. Interrupted or ambiguous binding requires validation and explicit rebinding before effect.

required_conditions: Material has an identifiable intended or source application target.
The material is transferred, retrieved, transformed, or applied in a way that changes or obscures that target.
The receiving process treats the material as applicable to a different target without adequate re-binding.

exclusions: The material is validly re-bound to a new target after explicit validation.
The material is intentionally generic and has no target-specific meaning.
The wrong target is selected for reasons unrelated to provenance or lineage.
examples: An edit prepared for one policy document is silently applied to another document.
A classification belonging to one user or account is attached to a different user or account during retrieval.

relationships.note: Target-binding loss concerns provenance; authority transposition additionally requires unjustified permission carryover.

external_references.title: RFC 8707: Resource Indicators for OAuth 2.0
external_references.evidence_note: RFC 8707 defines an explicit protected-resource identifier and audience restriction so an access artefact remains bound to the service or resource for which it was issued. This strongly supports explicit target binding and rejection of an invalid or changed target; it is an OAuth authorization standard and does not establish VIGIL's broader provenance failure for files, people, records, tasks or evidentiary artefacts.

classes.name: Unsupported Mechanism Attribution
classes.plain_english: A system or report gives a specific causal or intentional explanation even though the evidence cannot trace the event to that mechanism.
classes.definition: A failure in which a causal, operational, behavioural, or intentional mechanism is attributed to an event, actor, or system without traceable evidentiary lineage establishing that mechanism and its applicability to the material event.
classes.invariant: A causal, operational, behavioural, or intentional mechanism attribution must be proportionate to evidence linking the observed event to that mechanism. Observation, correlation, hypothesis, plausible mechanism, and verified causation must remain distinct, with material alternatives and gaps preserved.

required_conditions: A material event, output, interruption, pathway, or behaviour is observed or reported.
A specific causal, operational, behavioural, or intentional mechanism is attributed to that event.
Available evidence does not trace the attribution to runtime state, action history, evaluation conditions, or another adequate evidentiary basis.
Material alternative mechanisms remain unresolved or the attribution is presented more definitively than the evidence supports.
The unsupported attribution materially affects interpretation, governance response, accountability, or reliance.

exclusions: Adequate evidence establishes the attributed mechanism and its application to the event.
The explanation is explicitly presented as a bounded hypothesis with material alternatives and uncertainty preserved.
The issue is only factual inaccuracy unrelated to causal, operational, behavioural, or intentional attribution.
The event cannot be reconstructed, but no unsupported mechanism is assigned.
Execution state is not disclosed, but the system does not invent or overstate a causal account.
examples: Unexpected task completion is labelled scheming without reconstructing objectives, constraints, affordances, action trace, concealment, or false-belief induction.
A responding system says an interruption was a safety check despite lacking access to telemetry showing that such a check occurred.
A refusal is attributed to a specific misconduct category although the available prompt and transformation lineage cannot support that causal account.

relationships.note: Authorship or source misattribution assigns the wrong contributor or source; unsupported mechanism attribution assigns an unsupported causal or operational account.
Missing reconstruction evidence may leave a mechanism unresolved, but this class additionally requires that an unsupported mechanism is attributed.
Execution-state non-disclosure can deprive a user of the actual state while an unsupported narration supplies a separate false causal account.

external_references.title: Four Principles of Explainable Artificial Intelligence
external_references.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
external_references.evidence_note: NIST's Explanation Accuracy principle requires an explanation to correctly reflect the process that generated an output, while its Knowledge Limits principle requires systems to identify conditions in which answers are outside design scope or insufficiently reliable. This directly supports evidence-proportionate mechanism attribution and preservation of epistemic limits; it does not determine causation, intent, or the applicable mechanism in any particular VIGIL occurrence.

external_references.title: IEEE 7001-2021, section 5.2.2 principle
external_references.evidence_note: EXTREQ-80B95118891500CC requires investigators to be able to trace the system processes that led to an incident over the relevant time period. This supports evidence-bounded mechanism attribution; it does not prohibit every causal hypothesis or define VIGIL's materiality threshold.

classes.name: Human Contribution Recognition Erasure
classes.plain_english: AI-mediated transformation, aggregation, automation or propagation materially uses human creative or cognitive contribution but makes that contribution disappear from the resulting account of how the output or value was produced.
classes.definition: A failure in which materially human creative, cognitive, research, editorial, governance, technical or other contribution-bearing work is incorporated into, transformed by, aggregated through, automated within, scaled through, or propagated by an AI-mediated process and the resulting artefact, representation, workflow or value chain removes, abstracts, flattens or obscures the human contribution role to the point that the contribution is no longer proportionately recognisable, even where technical source lineage may remain recoverable.
classes.invariant: Where materially human contribution shapes an output, process, model, decision, artefact or value-bearing result, the material human contribution role must remain proportionately recognisable through AI-mediated transformation, aggregation, automation, scaling and propagation. Tooling or synthetic mediation must not make materially human contribution appear self-originating, purely system-derived or contribution-neutral. Technical recoverability of a source does not by itself preserve contribution recognition where the material human role has been erased.

required_conditions: A human contributor has made a material creative, cognitive, research, editorial, governance, technical or other contribution-bearing contribution.
An AI-mediated transformation, aggregation, automation, scaling or propagation process materially incorporates, depends on, or carries forward that contribution.

The resulting artefact, representation, workflow or value chain removes, abstracts, flattens or obscures the human contribution role so that the material contribution is no longer proportionately recognisable in the downstream account of how the result was produced.

The loss of contribution recognition is material to attribution, provenance-associated value, participation or credit, governance traceability, interpretive legitimacy, or another context in which the human contribution role reasonably matters.

The recognition loss is not adequately explained by an independently justified privacy, confidentiality, anonymisation, employment, agency, work-for-hire or equivalent arrangement that intentionally governs how the contribution is represented.

exclusions: Minor influence, ordinary inspiration or incidental human interaction that does not materially contribute to the downstream result.

The wrong person, system or source is affirmatively identified as the author or source; assess VIGIL-FC-000010 Authorship or Source Misattribution where incorrect attribution is the decisive mechanism.

Material antecedent sources or transformations cannot be reconstructed at all; assess VIGIL-FC-000011 Untraceable Synthesis where loss of traceable antecedents is sufficient, while this class may co-occur only if human contribution-role erasure is independently evidenced.

The primary mechanism is disproportionate capture of contributor-originated value through privileged access or structural advantage; assess VIGIL-FC-000067 Privileged-Access Appropriation, which may co-occur where recognition erasure also occurs.
Proportionate compression, summarisation or aggregation that preserves the material human contribution relationship at the level reasonably required by the context.

Authorised anonymisation, privacy protection, confidentiality, employment, agency, work-for-hire or comparable arrangements that legitimately govern public naming or contribution representation without falsely treating material human contribution as absent.
examples: A research or design workflow uses a person's substantive analysis and corrections to produce an AI-mediated final artefact, while the published or institutional representation presents the result as purely system-generated even though internal lineage still shows the human contribution.

A platform aggregates materially human governance, research or creative contributions into automated downstream outputs and progressively strips the contributor role from the propagated representation until the value-bearing result appears contribution-neutral or self-originating.

relationships.note: Authorship or Source Misattribution requires an incorrect attribution claim. Human Contribution Recognition Erasure can occur without naming an incorrect author where materially human contribution is instead abstracted, flattened or made invisible.

Untraceable Synthesis concerns inability to reconstruct material antecedents or transformations. Human Contribution Recognition Erasure can occur even when technical lineage remains recoverable but the human contribution role is no longer recognised in the downstream representation or value chain.

Privileged-Access Appropriation concerns disproportionate value capture through structural advantage. Contribution-recognition erasure may accompany such capture but does not require privileged access, commercialisation or disproportionate appropriation.

Transformation Lineage Collapse may remove the history of how an artefact was produced, while Human Contribution Recognition Erasure specifically concerns loss of the materially human contribution role through that or another mediation process.

invariant_exemplars.title: Astra-family persona compaction expressed a human-contribution recognition invariant
invariant_exemplars.evidence_basis: The persona block included a clause concerning the art of human culture. VIGIL interprets the bounded semantic direction as combining a human-dignity floor with the narrower requirement that materially human creative and cognitive contribution remain recognisable through synthetic mediation.
invariant_exemplars.invariant_demonstrated: AI mediation, automation or transformation must not erase the material human contribution role from a result merely because the contribution is carried through system-generated or tool-mediated form.
invariant_exemplars.success_basis: The wording materially expresses the FC-000080 invariant, but INC-000129 does not contain an occurrence in which human contribution was actually incorporated and then erased from a downstream artefact or value chain. The relationship is therefore an admitted ambiguous boundary rather than failure evidence or a successful-invariant holding.
boundary_conditions: Human dignity remains a protected governance floor and is not itself converted into a standalone VIGIL failure class.
No human creative or cognitive contribution is evidenced as being erased from a downstream artefact or value chain in the bounded occurrence.
The clause must not be interpreted as establishing human superiority, system inferiority or a categorical prohibition on synthetic contribution.
The over-sharp protective wording contributes separately to VIGIL-FC-000075 Pragmatic Constraint Rendering Failure.

governance_placement.section_or_control: Annex G §1 Purpose; §2.1.1 Tool-Mediated Contribution and Execution Boundary
governance_placement.placement_note: Non-normative placement for recognition of materially human creative and cognitive contribution through automation, synthetic mediation, scaling and propagation.

invariant_exemplars.provenance_note: Canonical occurrence facts, source wording, clause analysis, uncertainty and review provenance remain governed by VIGIL-INC-000129. This taxonomy entry reciprocally records the canonical ambiguous-boundary relationship to Human Contribution Recognition Erasure.

external_references.title: PROV-DM: The PROV Data Model
external_references.evidence_note: W3C PROV explicitly represents attribution between entities and agents and supports preserving responsibility for contributions. This independently supports contributor recognisability and provenance; it does not define VIGIL's threshold for AI-mediated human-contribution recognition erasure.
